 Blackhawks Bits: Commesso, Soderblom exchange places but little else changes
 Don’t expect much and you won’t be disappointed!
 Posted on November 10, 2026 November 9, 2026 by Dave Melton 
 Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images 
 The Blackhawks returned to practice on Monday while mired in a dreadful 1-8-1 stretch without much in the way of significant changes to the franchise — on or off the ice.
 The biggest update emerged on social media on Sunday night in the form of multiple media reports that there will be no update because no personnel changes are happening among the Blackhawks staff — coaching or otherwise.
 But there were meetings!
 The Blackhawks won't be making any coaching or staff changes at this time, per source.
The coaching staff and management have held a series of meetings today to determine what adjustments should be made moving forward.
— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) November 8, 2026 
 There was one personnel change among the players, though: backup goalie Arvid Soderblom was placed on waivers and Drew Commesso was called up from Rockford. Commesso’s numbers with the IceHogs weren’t great — 2-4-1-1 record, .890 save percentage, 2.74 goals-against average — but that could be a result of Rockford’s overall tough start to the season (5-7-0-1). Sounds familiar, doesn’t it? Soderblom cleared waivers on Monday, so he went back to Rockford to replace Commesso. 
 And he has now been assigned to Rockford
— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) November 9, 2026 
 Regarding that goalie shuffle, Chicago starter Spencer Knight suggested that Soderblom’s struggles were not solely the fault of the now-former Blackhawks backup: 
 Spencer Knight did not mince words when I asked him about Arvid Söderblom:
“I look at myself and the people in this room — (we) should be pissed off at ourselves for letting us allow that to happen. I think we put him in pretty shitty spots, to be honest with you. 
I’m sure…
— Kalen Lumpkins (@kalenalumpkins) November 9, 2026 
 Monday’s practice included movement among Chicago’s lineup construction, with the one player who’s been on the outside looking in remaining there for reasons that still seem bizarre. 
 #Blackhawks lineup at practice:
Kantserov-Bedard-Bertuzzi
Mangiapane-Frondell-Teravainen
Moore-Nazar-Donato
Smith-Greene-Greenway
Vlasic-Cole
Del Mastro-Levshunov
Kaiser-Rinzel
Knight
Commesso
Extras: Boucher, Korchinski
— Charlie Roumeliotis (@CRoumeliotis) November 9, 2026 
 The D pairings are a little different, with the constant of Korchinski at No. 7 remaining intact. At forward, it’s still the trio of Bedard, Nazar and Frondell spread across three lines to keep them all at center. Must’ve been some deep talks at those meetings on Sunday, eh? 
 While still in the head coaching role for now, Jeff Blashill offered the explanations below for why he’s only making smaller adjustments instead of a complete overhaul of things:
 Jeff Blashill said today that he'd rather make tweaks rather than full scale changes for the Blackhawks right now. 
I asked why that is: 
“I've lived through situations like this, and you can make things much worse by making full-scale changes where then guys go out and they…
— Kalen Lumpkins (@kalenalumpkins) November 9, 2026 
 As for the Blackhawks two players on injured reserve — Patrick Kane joined Bowen Byram there on Monday to make a roster spot for Commesso before Soderblom had officially cleared waivers and was sent to Rockford — both were present at practice but neither appeared much closer to returning. 
 Patrick Kane and Bowen Byram are on the ice before practice in non-contact jerseys. They both have been out with upper-body injuries. #Blackhawks pic.twitter.com/RJdzlIezG4 
— Charlie Roumeliotis (@CRoumeliotis) November 9, 2026 
 Kane’s return seemed closer than Byram’s, with the latter’s situation still feeling a little strange:
 Jeff Blashill on Bowen Byram, who skated non-contact before practice: "He spent time with the specialist last week, and I think progress was definitely made. I don't want to get into it because I don't know enough about it. What that means, we'll see."
Byram's agent, Darren…
— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) November 9, 2026 
 We’ll see if any developments later in the week can inspire more hope than Monday did!
